dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies, state and local governments, public housing agencies, banks, credit unions, mortgage lenders, developers, landlords, veterans, and millions of housing program participants nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: This act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs.

dimensions.assessment: Substantial changes to housing availability, loan limits, banking deposit rules, appraisal standards, disaster recovery funding, and restrictions on large institutional property purchases.
dimensions.evidence: To increase the supply of housing in America, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations such as $200 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for the Innovation Fund, modifies federal loan maximums, creates grant programs, and alters CDBG and disaster recovery fund allocations.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $200,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031.

dimensions.assessment: Amends multiple major federal statutes including the National Housing Act, Housing and Community Development Act, Cranston-Gonzalez National Affordable Housing Act, Federal Deposit Insurance Act, and the Federal Credit Union Act.
dimensions.evidence: This act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent changes to statutes alongside temporary pilot programs, reporting requirements, and sunset dates spanning up to 15 years or longer across the United States.
dimensions.evidence: This act may be cited as the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act.

importance_detail.rationale: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act is sweeping legislation that establishes and modifies numerous federal housing programs, alters banking and deposit rules, amends environmental review requirements, updates FHA loan limits and manufactured housing standards, and sets restrictions on large institutional investors purchasing single-family homes.

summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies federal housing programs and banking regulations to address housing supply, affordability, and regulatory hurdles. It creates pilot programs and grant initiatives for housing repairs, conversions of empty buildings, small-dollar mortgages, and manufactured housing without permanent chassis. It also adjusts environmental review rules under NEPA, alters bank investment limits, modifies the HOME Investment Partnerships program, and restricts the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency.

affected_groups.effect: Gain increased access to small-dollar mortgages, clearer disclosures regarding VA home loans, and support for home purchases through various grant programs.
Benefit from increased funding and revised eligibility for affordable housing, home repair grants, and community development block grants prioritizing vulnerable populations.
Face a prohibition on purchasing additional single-family homes if they control 350 or more single-family homes.
Benefit from increased public welfare investment caps, adjusted reciprocal deposit rules, and modified supervisory testing thresholds.
Eligible to apply for competitive grants relating to housing plans, building code guidelines for point-access block buildings, and disaster recovery assistance.

key_provisions: Establishes a whole-home repairs pilot program offering grants to homeowners and forgivable loans to eligible landlords to update properties for accessibility, habitability, and energy efficiency.
Authorizes HUD to establish a four-year pilot program to increase access to small-dollar mortgages of $100,000 or less and adjusts FHA multifamily loan limits.
Permits the construction of manufactured homes without a permanent chassis, subject to new standards and state certifications.
Exempts certain residential housing construction on infill sites from environmental reviews under NEPA to streamline development.
Increases the allowable aggregate public welfare investments for national and state member banks from 15% to 20% of capital stock and surplus.
Prohibits large institutional investors holding 350 or more single-family homes from purchasing additional single-family homes, with specific exceptions.
Prohibits the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Federal reserve banks from issuing a central bank digital currency or substantially similar asset.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts appropriated for carrying out the various grants and pilot programs, as section 1202 states no additional funds are authorized.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies federal housing programs and banking regulations to address housing supply, affordability, and regulatory hurdles. It creates pilot programs and grant initiatives for housing repairs, conversions of empty buildings, small-dollar mortgages, and manufactured housing without permanent chassis. It also adjusts environmental review rules under NEPA, alters bank investment limits, modifies the HOME Investment Partnerships program, and restricts the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency.
summary_detail.significance: The Act introduces wide-ranging structural modifications to federal housing, banking, and disaster recovery policy. It impacts the supply of housing by streamlining environmental reviews, altering local zoning guidance frameworks, modifying financing limits for manufactured and multifamily housing, and altering operations for community banks and public housing agencies.
